title: Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh in winter: which is better?
author: Matt
intro: Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh are Egypt's two big Red Sea resorts, and in winter they're both warm, sunny and about five hours from the UK. Sharm has the more famous reefs and is a degree or two warmer. Hurghada is bigger, often cheaper and puts Luxor within reach. Here's how to choose.
seo_title: Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh in winter? Compared
seo_description: Sharm is a little warmer with better reefs. Hurghada is bigger, often cheaper and closer to Luxor. Winter weather, snorkelling, day trips and flights.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warmer:** Sharm, by a degree or so
- **Best reefs:** Sharm and Ras Mohammed
- **Best for Luxor:** Hurghada, about 4 hrs
- **Flight time:** about 5 to 5½ hrs

Both are good choices for winter sun, and the difference is smaller than people think. Pick Sharm if snorkelling and diving matter most. Pick Hurghada if you want more variety, a day at the ancient sites of Luxor or a better-value week.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.text:
| | [Sharm el-Sheikh](/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh) | [Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| December high | about 24°C | about 23°C |
| January high | about 22°C | about 21°C |
| February high | about 23°C | about 22°C |
| Where it is | southern tip of the Sinai | the Red Sea coast of mainland Egypt |
| Best known for | reefs and snorkelling | islands, wrecks and Luxor trips |
| Feel | resort areas around bays | a long strip of hotels and a real town |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our guides. Both are sunny almost every day in winter, but evenings are much cooler, so bring a jumper. Both are two hours ahead of the UK.

sections.heading: The sea, reefs and diving
sections.text:
This is the biggest difference between the two:

- **Sharm el-Sheikh** sits beside Ras Mohammed National Park and the Straits of Tiran, with some of the most famous coral reefs in the world. Many hotels have their own house reef, so you can snorkel straight off the jetty.
- **Hurghada** has good reefs too, but the best ones are mostly a boat ride away, around the Giftun Islands. It's known for wreck diving, including the reefs and wrecks at Abu Nuhas.

The famous Thistlegorm wreck lies in between, and dive boats run there from both resorts. In winter, the sea is around 21 to 23°C, slightly warmer in Sharm. That's fine for snorkelling on a sunny day, but many divers wear a thicker wetsuit.

Tip: if you plan to snorkel every day, choose a Sharm hotel with a good house reef. It makes far more difference than which resort you pick.

sections.heading: Things to do beyond the beach
sections.text:
- **From Hurghada:** a day trip to **Luxor**, about four hours each way by road, for the Valley of the Kings and Karnak Temple. It's a long day but a memorable one. **El Gouna**, a lagoon town of canals and restaurants, is about 30 minutes north.
- **From Sharm:** desert safaris with quad bikes and Bedouin dinners, the Old Market, and the lively promenade at Naama Bay. Night trips to climb **Mount Sinai** for sunrise run from Sharm, but it's a long, cold night in winter.

If seeing ancient Egypt is high on your list, Hurghada is the easier base. Trips to Cairo and Luxor from Sharm are possible but much longer, and usually involve a flight.

sections.heading: Flights, visas and travel advice
sections.text:
- **Flights:** both have direct winter flights from many UK airports with Jet2, easyJet and TUI. Sharm and Hurghada are each about five to five and a half hours away.
- **Visas:** UK visitors normally need a visa for Egypt, available as an e-visa or on arrival. Sharm has long offered a free Sinai-only entry stamp for short stays in the South Sinai resorts, but you need a full visa to travel further, so check the current rules before you go.
- **Travel advice:** the UK Foreign Office advises against travel to parts of the Sinai peninsula, but not to Sharm el-Sheikh or the Red Sea coast resorts. Check GOV.UK's latest Egypt advice before you book, as it can change.

Watch out: Egypt's tourist areas have security checks on roads and at hotels. They're routine, but leave extra time when you're heading to the airport.

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.text:
- **Choose Sharm el-Sheikh** for the best snorkelling and diving, slightly warmer weather and a calm resort week by the reef.
- **Choose Hurghada** for a bigger choice of hotels and prices, island boat trips, El Gouna and a day at Luxor.
- **For families:** both work well. Look for a sandy beach, a calm bay and a heated pool, as the sea can feel fresh in January.

Still can't decide? Put both on a shared list in somewhere.party, give everyone points to vote with, and let the draw choose. For more winter ideas, see [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) or our [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) post for somewhere closer to UK time.

faqs.question: Is Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: Sharm el-Sheikh is usually a degree or so warmer, at about 22 to 24°C by day from December to February. Hurghada is about 21 to 23°C. Both are sunny, with cool evenings.

faqs.question: Which is better for snorkelling, Hurghada or Sharm?
faqs.answer: Sharm el-Sheikh, especially at hotels with their own house reef and on trips to Ras Mohammed and Tiran. Hurghada's best reefs are mostly reached by boat.

faqs.question: Can you visit Luxor from Sharm el-Sheikh?
faqs.answer: It's possible but a long trip, usually with a flight. From Hurghada, Luxor is about four hours by road, so it's a popular day trip.

faqs.question: Is it safe to go to Sharm el-Sheikh?
faqs.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against travel to parts of the Sinai, but not to Sharm el-Sheikh itself. Check GOV.UK's latest Egypt travel advice before you book and before you travel.
